title: Propositional Horn clauses: forward chaining and least models
summary: Propagate the conclusions of Horn rules, prove a finite stopping bound, and decide satisfiability by checking constraints in the least candidate model.
abstract: If a switch is on, a lamp must light; if two sensors trigger, an alarm must sound. Requirements with one possible positive conclusion can be checked by repeatedly adding the conclusions whose premises are already true. Starting with no true atoms, this process finds all the atoms forced by the rules with an atomic conclusion. We prove that finitely many rounds suffice and that the resulting assignment is contained in every model. Rules forbidding a combination of true atoms can then be checked against this single assignment. Cyclic rules and contradictory requirements show why a permitted conclusion need not be a forced one, and why constraints must still be checked. For a finite atom set, the converse also holds: precisely the intersection-closed families of valuations are definable by Horn rules, and definite rules additionally require the all-true valuation.
